content:
Compared the two runs window-by-window (same model, `OlmoEarth-v1-FT-AWF-Base` rev `a347b15`; A = C1/2023, B = C2/2022, both covering all 16,384 windows of the area).

**Where they differ:** 3,807 of 16,384 windows (23.2%). They concentrate in the north: 39.4% of differences fall in the top quarter of the grid (row band 0, rows 0–31), and 34.0% in the western column band. Most sit on predicted-class boundaries (78.3% of differing windows touch a boundary). The dominant change direction is **grassland_barren in map A → shrubland_savanna in map B** (1,409 windows, 37.0%; the reverse only 268), then montane_forest→woodland_forest (447) and woodland_forest→shrubland_savanna (388). All 3,807 differing windows are listed in `.../workspace/compare_differing_df789c0586.json`.

**Which is right: not determinable.** The maps describe different years (2022 vs 2023), so any difference may be real ground change rather than an error in one map — no recorded experiment grades this pair, and without dated reference labels neither side can be declared correct. Note also that B (2022) has the larger logit margin on 57.8% of differing windows, but the more-confident side is not thereby the right one.

If you have labels for either date, pass them (e.g. as `labels_date`) and I can grade each map against its own reference to separate true change from errors.
